evidence.claim: AC2's bypass is real: http://2130706433/ is ACCEPTED by the current validator (isIpLiteral's regex only matches 1-3-digit dotted quads, so InetAddress is never consulted).
evidence.source: Ran the compiled UrlValidator from service/target/classes: new UrlValidator("localhost").parseOrThrow+requireShortenable("http://2130706433/") -> ACCEPTED (host=2130706433). Code at UrlValidator.java:47,152-154.

evidence.claim: AC1's bypass is real: https://malware.example.com./x is ACCEPTED — URI.getHost() keeps the trailing dot and DenylistThreatCheck's parentOf walk ("malware.example.com." -> "example.com." -> "com.") never equals the seeded row 'malware.example.com'.
evidence.source: Same probe -> ACCEPTED (host=malware.example.com.); DenylistThreatCheck.java:49-62; V2__seed_customers_and_denylist.sql:29-32.

evidence.claim: The trailing dot also defeats the internal-host check, not just the denylist: http://LOCALHOST./ is ACCEPTED today while http://localhost/ is 422. Normalisation therefore closes two holes, and lower-casing alone closes neither.
evidence.source: Probe output: 'http://LOCALHOST./ ACCEPTED' vs 'http://localhost/ URL_REJECTED 422'; UrlValidator.java:104-123.

evidence.claim: Three forms the impact analysis lists as 'accepted today' are in fact already refused, with 400 invalid_request rather than 201: http://127.1/, http://0x7f.0.0.1/ and http://例え.テスト/ (java.net.URI returns a null host for each, so parseOrThrow throws at the syntax stage).
evidence.source: Probe output: each -> INVALID_REQUEST 400 {longUrl=must be an absolute http or https URL}; UrlValidator.java:93-95.

evidence.claim: IPv4-mapped IPv6 is NOT a bypass — it is already refused: http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/ and http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/ both answer 422 today, because isIpLiteral matches '[' and InetAddress unwraps the mapping.
evidence.source: Probe output: both -> URL_REJECTED 422; UrlValidator.java:114,152-154.

evidence.claim: Two further live bypasses exist beyond AC2's example: http://0x7f000001/ and http://017700000001/ and http://0177.0.0.1/ are all ACCEPTED today, and glibc resolves all three to 127.0.0.1.

A normaliser built on InetAddress.getByName will not work on JDK 21: getByName('0x7f000001') and ('017700000001') throw UnknownHostException, and getByName('0177.0.0.1') returns 177.0.0.1 — a public address — where curl reaches 127.0.0.1. The IPv4 forms must be parsed by hand.
evidence.source: Direct probe on openjdk 21.0.12: 0177.0.0.1 -> 177.0.0.1 loopback=false; 0x7f000001 and 017700000001 -> UnknownHostException; 2130706433 and 127.1 -> 127.0.0.1.

evidence.claim: The servlet filter mapping claim holds: '/api/v1/*' is a prefix mapping that covers /api/v1/public/links and /api/v1/customers, so both new endpoints ARE filtered unless explicitly exempted. Trailing-slash ('/api/v1/sessions/') and double-slash ('/api/v1//public/links') variants also stay filtered, i.e. shouldNotFilter's exact-equality comparison fails closed.
evidence.source: Ran an embedded Tomcat 10.1.55 (from ~/.m2) with a servlet at '/' and a filter mapped '/api/v1/*': /api/v1/public/links filtered=true, /api/v1/customers filtered=true, /api/v1/sessions/ filtered=true, /api/v1//public/links filtered=true, /abc123 filtered=false. Matches WebConfig.java:28,36 and SessionAuthenticationFilter.java:52-54.

evidence.claim: IP-keyed limiting for the two new endpoints needs no new plumbing: RateLimitGuard.requireByAddress(bucket, address) already exists and SignInController already calls it with httpRequest.getRemoteAddr().
evidence.source: RateLimitGuard.java:27-29; SignInController.java:36-42.

evidence.claim: Adding a bucket is compile-safe: capacityOf() is an exhaustive switch over RateLimitBucket, so a new value fails the build until it is mapped to a property; keys are namespaced 'ratelimit:<bucket>:<key>', so a new bucket cannot spend WRITE tokens.
evidence.source: RedisTokenBucketRateLimiter.java capacityOf switch and keyFor().

evidence.claim: The limiter fails open on a Redis fault (logs a WARN and returns ALLOWED), so during a Redis outage the anonymous create path and sign-up are unmetered; a sign-up costs a measured 25.6 ms and 16 MiB of Argon2id work per request on this machine (m=16384,t=2,p=1).
evidence.source: RedisTokenBucketRateLimiter.java catch(RuntimeException) -> RateLimitDecision.ALLOWED; timed Argon2PasswordEncoder.defaultsForSpringSecurity_v5_8() from spring-security-crypto 6.5.11: hash avg 25.6 ms, verify avg 24.1 ms; Argon2PasswordHasher.java:22.

evidence.claim: No existing test fixture uses any evasion form (numeric IPv4, hex/octal, trailing dot), so the AC3 tests are net-new and no current expectation contradicts the fix.
evidence.source: ripgrep over service/src for 2130706433|0x7f|127\.1|example\.com\. — zero matches in src/test; Fixtures.java:54-78 lists the only target constants.

evidence.claim: No test pins the size or contents of the ErrorCode enum, so adding a value (Q2's 409 account_unavailable) breaks no existing assertion; only openapi.yaml's closed catalogue table and info.version need to move with it.
evidence.source: ripgrep 'ErrorCode|values\(\)|catalogue' over service/src/test -> one prose mention in DegradedDependencyTest.java:226; artifacts/openapi.yaml:5 (version 1.0.0), :47-59 (catalogue table).

evidence.claim: Hibernate's schema validation checks column existence and type only — not nullability. An old instance whose LinkEntity still declares customer_id nullable=false will start against the migrated (nullable) schema, so schema-first rollout is safe.
evidence.source: javap -c on org.hibernate.tool.schema.internal.AbstractSchemaValidator (hibernate-core 6.6.53.Final): validateColumnType calls only ColumnDefinitions.hasMatchingType and raises 'wrong column type encountered'; no nullability branch. LinkEntity.java:165.

evidence.claim: AC8/AC13 hold by construction with a NULL owner: every owner-scoped query is an equality match on customerId and nothing joins links to customers, so NULL rows match no customer's reads.
evidence.source: LinkRepository.java:28 (findByDomainAndCodeAndCustomerId) and :38-39 (findOwnedBy JPQL 'where l.customerId = :customerId'); the click path uses findByDomainAndCode (:25), which is unscoped.

evidence.claim: The shared normaliser can be added without touching the ThreatCheck port: check(URI) already receives the URL and DenylistThreatCheck does its own lower-casing internally, so it can call the same normaliser; NoOpThreatCheck and ThreatCheckConfig stay untouched.
evidence.source: ThreatCheck.java (interface method check(URI)); DenylistThreatCheck.java:33-39; ThreatCheckConfig.java:12-15.

evidence.claim: A11's 'alias/expiresAt answer 400' requires a NEW request record: CreateLinkRequest declares alias and expiresAt as known properties, so reusing it on the anonymous endpoint would silently accept both rather than triggering the strict-body 400.
evidence.source: CreateLinkRequest.java:24-27; spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties: true in application.yml:46-51.

evidence.claim: customers today has a plain case-sensitive UNIQUE(email) and no functional index, and CustomerEntity exposes only a protected no-arg constructor — so sign-up needs both a migration and a real constructor.
evidence.source: V1__initial_schema.sql:11-19 (CONSTRAINT ux_customers_email UNIQUE (email)); CustomerEntity.java:231-233; CustomerRepository.findByEmailIgnoreCase.

evidence.claim: The test suite never truncates PostgreSQL — only Redis is flushed, and only when a test calls resetSharedTierState(). Sign-up rows therefore accumulate across the whole JVM-wide suite, so duplicate/uniqueness tests must mint unique emails or they collide with earlier tests rather than with the code under test.
evidence.source: AbstractIntegrationTest.java:295-299 (flushDb only); TestInfrastructure.java:45-59 (JVM-wide singleton containers); ripgrep for truncate/deleteAll over service/src -> no matches.

evidence.claim: Limitation of this spike: the Docker socket is not reachable from here (permission denied), so nothing requiring a live PostgreSQL/Redis was executed — the migration behaviour, the lower(email) index and the full suite are unverified by run and rest on code reading plus the bytecode/servlet probes above.
evidence.source: docker images / docker ps -> 'permission denied while trying to connect to the docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock'.

options.summary: Normalise inside UrlValidator.requireShortenable and DenylistThreatCheck only (one shared HostNormalizer, hand-rolled IPv4 parsing, trailing-dot strip, lower-case, IDN ToASCII). parseOrThrow is untouched, so the current 400s for hosts java.net.URI cannot parse stay 400. Fixes both AC1 and AC2 examples plus the hex/octal/short-decimal forms that do parse.
Extract the host from URI.getAuthority() ahead of the syntax gate so every equivalent form — including 127.1, 0x7f.0.0.1 and unicode IDN — reaches host policy and answers 422 url_rejected.
Option 1 plus a narrow rule: when an authority is present but URI.getHost() is null, answer 422 rather than 400 (fail closed on unparseable hosts without re-deriving the host ourselves).

unknowns.current_best_answer: Keep them 400. They are already refused, no AC needs 422, and leaving parseOrThrow untouched keeps the blast radius to the two forms the ACs name.
unknowns.how_to_settle: One sentence from the requester or architect: 'refused with 400 is good enough for forms the URL parser cannot read' vs 'every equivalent form must be 422'. Reproduce the current behaviour with: javac/java against service/target/classes calling new UrlValidator("localhost").parseOrThrow("http://127.1/") — prints INVALID_REQUEST 400.
unknowns.question: Must target forms that java.net.URI cannot parse as a host (http://127.1/, http://0x7f.0.0.1/, http://例え.テスト/, http://malware.example.com../) answer 422 url_rejected, or is today's 400 invalid_request refusal acceptable for them?
unknowns.why_it_matters: I ran the real UrlValidator: those forms are already refused today, but at the syntax stage with 400 (URI.getHost() returns null). Assumption A1 lists 'short forms 127.1' and IDN as in scope and A3 says an unnormalisable host must be 422 — honouring that literally means moving host extraction ahead of parseOrThrow's null-host check, which changes a documented 400 into a 422 on the frozen contract and touches the exact 400-vs-422 split the regression surface pins. Neither AC1 nor AC2 requires it: both of their examples parse fine and are fixed by normalising inside requireShortenable/DenylistThreatCheck alone.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Yes — hand-parse decimal/octal/hex/short IPv4 per the WHATWG host parser and never delegate canonicalisation to InetAddress.getByName; feed the resulting 4 bytes to the existing isInternalAddress predicate.
unknowns.how_to_settle: Confirm with the requester that the threat model is 'what the client will actually connect to'. Verified divergence: python3 -c "import socket; print(socket.getaddrinfo('0177.0.0.1',80)[0][4])" -> 127.0.0.1, while Java InetAddress.getByName("0177.0.0.1") -> 177.0.0.1 and getByName("0x7f000001") -> UnknownHostException.
unknowns.question: Does 'equivalent form' mean the browser/curl reading of numeric IPv4 (0177.0.0.1, 0x7f000001, 017700000001 all = 127.0.0.1), even though JDK 21 reads 0177.0.0.1 as the public address 177.0.0.1 and refuses the other two outright?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Getting this wrong in either direction is expensive. Building the normaliser on InetAddress.getByName (the obvious implementation) silently leaves hex and long-octal loopback forms accepted, and actively mis-canonicalises 0177.0.0.1 to a public address — so the fix looks done and the bypass is still open. Hand-parsing all four forms is the only way to match what a click actually reaches, and it must be specified before the test author (blind branch) writes AC2 assertions.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Unknown. In-repo there are exactly two customers (V2__seed_customers_and_denylist.sql:13-21), alice@ and bob@, no case variants.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Keep 10/min as the default (an order of magnitude under write-per-minute, per Q4), freeze the property name in AppProperties so the blind test branch can lower/raise it, and record the shared-bucket consequence in the runbook.
unknowns.how_to_settle: One sentence from whoever owns the deployment: is the service behind a proxy that preserves the client address? If not, agree the number is a global rate and pick it accordingly.
unknowns.question: Is 10/min per client IP the intended production default for anonymous creation, knowing it is a single shared bucket behind any proxy that does not preserve the source address?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Q5 settled that getRemoteAddr stays, so behind an LB the default is a global ceiling, not a per-caller one — the anonymous endpoint is then effectively closed under real traffic. It also interacts with the suite: every test hits from 127.0.0.1, one Redis is shared JVM-wide and only tests that call resetSharedTierState() flush it, so a default this tight makes anonymous-creation tests cross-couple unless they override the property.

unknowns.current_best_answer: Keep it — it identifies the created resource and costs nothing — but document explicitly in openapi.yaml that no GET exists for it, so nobody writes a client that follows it.
unknowns.how_to_settle: Yes/no from the API owner: keep the Location as a pure identifier, or omit it and return {customerId, email, createdAt} only.
unknowns.question: Sign-up returns Location: /api/v1/customers/{id} (Q7) — should it, given that path has no GET handler and is inside the session filter, so every caller including the new owner gets 401 or 405 from it?
unknowns.why_it_matters: It is the same objection Q9 used to drop the Location header from anonymous creation. A Location that never resolves is a contract statement that will be documented in openapi.yaml and asserted by a blind test author, and removing it later is a contract change rather than an edit.
